In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of antimitotic agents which inhibit the assembly and disassembly of tubulin and which inhibit the binding of vinca alkaloids to tubulin, thereby inhibiting the growth of cancer cells.
the development of a new antimitotic agent with a novel mode of action and with the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of action of this agent.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dolastatin 1 0 inhibits tubulin polymerization through its dolaproine residue and inhibits other ligand interactions through its dolaphenine residue.
the dolaproine segment and the C(6) position in dolaphenine are important for cytotoxicity and effects on ligand binding, and the dolavaline segment is important for polymerization inhibition.
dolastatin 1 is a tubulin ligand which inhibits tubulin polymerization and also inhibits other tubulin ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dolaproine segment is the critical segment for cytotoxicity and for effects on vinblastin binding and nucleotide exchange, and the dolaphenone segment is the critical region for effects on beta s cross-link and colchicine-binding activity.
dolastatin 1 0 has a complex mechanism of action, involving at least two distinct binding sites in tubulin, with the C(19a)-isomer binding site having the higher affinity.
the dolaproine and/or dolaphenine moieties are essential for the cytotoxicity and the other effects of dolastatin on tubulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxic activity of dolastatin analogs is correlated with their ability to bind strongly to tubulin, but that this binding is not sufficient to inhibit polymerization.
the dolaproine residue of dolastatin is essential for cytotoxicity and for inhibition of tubulin interactions with vinblastine, GTP, and colchicines.
dolastatin 20, a pentapeptide analog with reduced cytotoxic activity, is a good lead compound for development of new antimitotic agents.
